hook_text: A plank, a rope, a curve and a diving board. That is every bridge ever built.
clip_script: There are only a few ways to get across a gap. One: a beam. A plank across. It bends, top squashed, bottom stretched. Stand it on edge and it is sixty times stiffer, and if you hollow out the middle you get the I-beam. Good to about fifty metres. Two: a suspension bridge. Drape big cables over towers and hang the road from them. Cables pull, towers push, giant blocks on the shore hold the ends. Longest spans in the world. Three: cable-stayed. Cables straight from road to tower like a harp. Nelson Mandela Bridge, Johannesburg. Four: an arch. A curve squashed all the way round, so stone can do it. Bloukrans Bridge, 216 metres above the river. Five: a cantilever. A diving board, fixed at one end, bending hardest at the wall. Next bridge you cross, name it.
visual_style: Five quick whiteboard silhouettes: plank bending, draped cables over towers, harp-string fan, stone arch with thrust arrows, diving board with a root arrow; a South African label under three of them.
pacing: Five types at about ten seconds each, a one-line challenge to close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sort five bridge photos into the five types.
